ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the PRC (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024); Regulations for the Administration of Foreign Investment (2019, effective 1 January 2020); Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act (as amended) for source-entity screening.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization route for Taiwan-origin document: Taiwan court-affiliated notary public certification; Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification; Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) channel to competent Mainland Notary Association seal confirmation. Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille state; do not add an Apostille and do not chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / valid registration certificate of investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Office, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization route for Taiwan-origin document: Taiwan notary public certification; SEF verification; Mainland Notary Association authentication through ARATS channel. No Apostille possible; never apply Hague Apostille. Valid for filing with SAMR and local authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney for incorporation and UBO disclosure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan investing entity (legalized corporate authorization)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization route: board resolution authenticated by Taiwan notary public, with notarized specimen signatures and MOEA certification of board member authority; SEF verification; Mainland Notary Association confirmation through ARATS channel. Apostille unavailable in Taiwan; use only consular/cross-strait path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles) of investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, certified true copy of the Taiwan company registry record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization route: MOEA certified copy notarized by Taiwan notary; SEF verification; Mainland Notary Association authentication through ARATS channel. Never Apostilled; Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from investor's relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investor's relationship bank (e.g., first-class Taiwan commercial bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization route: bank officer signature and seal notarized by Taiwan notary; SEF verification; Mainland Notary Association authentication through ARATS channel; bank letter also independently validated by the receiving PRC bank under AML KYC. No Hague Apostille applies.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct enhanced due diligence on every shareholder, director, beneficial owner, authorized signatory and material counterparty against the PBOC/SAMR beneficial owner registry, the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and MOFCOM unreliable entity list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list including the 50% ownership rule, and the Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act lists. Politically exposed persons include domestic and foreign PEPs, immediate family members, and close associates, as well as senior officials from Taiwan public entities; all PEP relationships require senior management approval, source-of-wealth verification, ongoing transaction monitoring, and immediate re-screening upon sanctions list updates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Reservation and Registration System (State Administration for Market Regulation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in simplified Chinese characters and follow the four-tier structure: administrative division, distinct name (minimum two characters), industry or business description, and organizational form 'Limited Liability Company'. English names are not registered as statutory names and may be used only as a trade name after registration. Names derived from a Taiwan investor must use an approved phonetic transliteration converted from traditional characters into simplified Chinese according to SAMR transliteration conventions. No suffix such as 'Taiwan branch' may appear unless the entity is actually a branch; the WFOE shall not use words implying sovereignty or official status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 60 days of receiving a written name-rejection notice from SAMR, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the next higher market regulation authority, or bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months. The appeal must cite the reservation application number, the exact rejected Chinese name, the supporting proof of non-conflicting trademark or trade name, and any ministerial approval obtained for sensitive tokens. Before filing, the applicant should correct the name to remove prohibited tokens and resubmit through the same portal, reserving all appeal rights. Delays beyond the 30-day reservation window require a fresh application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered address for a PRC WFOE engaged in OOG project-cargo heavy-haul logistics. SAMR and the municipal tax bureau require a physical lease, proof of property ownership or lease filing, and actual management presence for receipt of legal documents, tax notices, and court service. Bank AML/KYC account-opening procedures will reject a mailbox address because logistics service invoices require a valid physical place of business. Certain free-trade zones allow 'nominated registered address' only for investment platforms, not for operating logistics companies; a managed shared office may be accepted only if there is a permanent employee, a lease of at least 12 months, and a distinct office/property identification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 68% during the first 18 months after incorporation. Unannounced physical inspections by the municipal SAMR and tax bureau are triggered by VAT invoice patterns, payroll registration, and office lease reporting. Inspection checklist: original business license at premises, current lease and rent payment records, social insurance and individual income tax filings, books and vouchers, project-cargo transportation contracts, subcontractor licenses, logistics site/yard lease if applicable, and presence of a responsible manager. Failure to satisfy these items can lead to removal from the address, loss of 'actual place of operation' status, tax registration cancellation, and administrative penalties.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 24-26, 32-38, 43-47, 50-59, 68-70, 83; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6, 7, 12, 15, 16, 17, 24, 28; Regulation of the People's Republic of China on the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law (2020), Articles 3, 5, 8, 14, 15, 19, 20; Interim Regulations on the Registration Management of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746, 2021), Articles 4, 8, 9, 10, 16, 17
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (MSA) with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online through the SAMR enterprise registration portal and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Market Entity Establishment Registration Application for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Liability Company (Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration Form)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital applies to this general logistics WFOE. The registered capital must be a fixed monetary amount set out in the Articles of Association, and each shareholder subscription must be fully paid within five years after the date of establishment under the 2024 Company Law. There is no blocked escrow account requirement under PRC law for ISIC 5229 freight and project cargo coordination services; however, capital contributions from the Taiwan investor must be remitted lawfully through a bank after completion of State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) foreign direct investment registration, and funds withdrawn must be used only for lawful corporate business purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at a duly convened inaugural meeting of the Board of Directors / Executive Director of [Company Name] (the Company), held by virtual meeting with the sole foreign investor's authorized representatives present, that the following formation and governance actions are unanimously adopted and declared immediately effective. A. Capital Subscription. The Company shall have a registered capital of [US$____ / RMB____] subscribed by the sole Taiwanese shareholder in cash. The Board accepts the subscription schedule attached as Annex A, and directs the legal representative and Chief Financial Officer to open a capital contribution bank account with [Bank] and to remit the initial paid-in tranche as required by the PRC Company Law, ensuring full payment of all subscriptions within five years after the date of issuance of the business license. The CFO shall execute all foreign exchange purchase and cross-border remittance documents under SAFE rules and shall not release capital except for lawful business purposes. B. Registered Office. The registered office shall be at [address], within the administrative jurisdiction of the Market Supervision Administration where the business license is issued. The legal representative is authorized to lease the office, settle all utilities, and file the lease, property ownership certificate, and landlord consent with the enterprise registration dossier. C. Banking Authorization. The Company shall establish its principal banking relationship with [Bank], [branch]. The Board authorizes [Name], General Manager, and [Name], CFO, to act as authorized signatories, each with dual-signature authority for all payments above [amount], all payments abroad, and all letters of credit. The bank account opening documents, signature cards, and online banking mandates may be executed by the authorized signatories without further Board action. D. Statutory Officers. The Board appoints [Name] as Executive Director / President and legal representative, [Name] as General Manager, and [Name] as CFO / Supervisor, with corresponding statutory duties and delegated powers to sign all filings, contracts, licenses, and registrations. E. General Delegation. All officers and the registered agent are authorized to execute and submit every registration, tax, social insurance, customs, foreign exchange, and logistics license application and to pay all fees, provided that any action exceeding [threshold amount] requires prior Board resolution. This resolution shall remain in full force until superseded by an amended resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Reservation, Business Scope Alignment, and Taiwan Investor Document Legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Registration Portal and the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (MSA) with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing the establishment application, the Taiwanese corporate investor must deliver a notarized certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, board resolution authorizing the investment, passport or business registration copies, and a power of attorney; these documents must be authenticated through the ARATS-SEF cross-strait authentication procedure. Concurrently, use the SAMR online name reservation platform to pre-approve the proposed company name, which must be arranged as locality plus trade name plus industry characteristic plus Limited Company, and must not conflict with existing trademarks or registered enterprise names. Upload the lease agreement, landlord property certificate, and draft Articles of Association on the same portal. The authority will issue a name reservation notice valid for the subsequent establishment filing period. If the name is rejected, the applicant must correct or substitute the name before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Notarized and ARATS-SEF authenticated certificate of incorporation of the Taiwan investor
Certificate of good standing of the Taiwan investor
Board resolution of the Taiwan parent authorizing the WFOE investment
Power of attorney appointing the local registration agent
Lease agreement for the registered office
Property ownership certificate or occupancy certificate of the registered office
Draft Articles of Association
Legal representative and supervisor identification copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, conduct a supplementary trade name search and reserve an alternative name; if the business scope is queried, narrow it to freight forwarding, project cargo coordination, and logistics support services, and add regulated transport activities only after obtaining separate permits; if the lease documents are challenged, provide a notarized landlord consent letter and re-upload within the validity period of the name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Corporate Governance Package and Capital Subscription Schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public and authentication institutions in Taiwan where required, followed by final filing preparation under the legal supervision of counsel; the local SAMR office will ultimately accept the governance package with the incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the final Chinese-language Articles of Association signed by all shareholders, the first shareholders resolution, the appointment certificate of the executive director or board members, the legal representative appointment, the supervisor appointment, the general manager appointment, and the written resolution approving bank signatories and the capital contribution schedule. All signatures of the Taiwan investor must be notarized in Taiwan and authenticated by ARATS-SEF prior to submission. The registered capital amount and the five-year contribution schedule must match the Foreign Investment Information Report and the ISIC 5229 project cargo heavy haul business scope. If the investor is a legal person, the parent company authorization and authenticated bylaw excerpts must be attached. The complete corporate governance package must remain unaltered from execution through SAMR filing.
required_dossiers: Final signed Articles of Association
Shareholders incorporation resolution
First board or executive director resolution
Capital subscription schedule
Legal representative appointment letter
General Manager appointment letter
Supervisor appointment letter
Notarized and ARATS-SEF authenticated signature specimens
Parent company investment board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If authentication is returned for correction, re-notarize the defective document and re-submit through the cross-strait authentication process; if the Articles are inconsistent with the business scope, amend the Articles by a supplemental shareholder resolution and re-execute before registration; if the local MSA requires a bilingual version, provide a sworn English translation with the Chinese text.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Market Entity Establishment Registration and Foreign Investment Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the integrated China enterprise registration portal or the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (MSA) window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Market Entity Establishment Registration Application together with the name pre-approval notice, authenticated Taiwan investor documents, final Articles of Association, lease and property certificate, identity copies of the legal representative and supervisors, and the negative-list self-assessment statement confirming that ISIC 5229 project cargo logistics is a permitted foreign investment industry. The registration system will simultaneously capture the Foreign Investment Information Report as part of the application. The MSA will review the legal representative eligibility, the capital schedule, and the business scope. If approved, the MSA issues the business license with the unified social credit code, registered capital, and the scope covering out-of-gauge and project cargo coordination, heavy-haul transport coordination, and related supporting services. After issuance, the registration is automatically publicized in the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
required_dossiers: Name pre-approval notice
Market Entity Establishment Registration Application form
Authenticated and notarized Taiwan investor documents
Final signed Articles of Association
Power of attorney for registration agent
Lease agreement and landlord title certificate
Legal representative and supervisor identity documents
Foreign Investment Information Report data submission
Negative-list self-assessment statement for ISIC 5229
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues an inquiry on the business scope or ownership structure, submit a written explanation and revised Articles within the response period; if the negative-list self-assessment is questioned, provide a legal opinion confirming that freight transportation arrangement is not in any restricted or prohibited foreign investment category; if the application is suspended due to information mismatch, correct the Foreign Investment Information Report and resubmit within the same application queue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation Statutory Registrations, Seal Carving, Bank Account Opening, Tax, Foreign Exchange, and Social Insurance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Public Security Bureau for seal engraving approval; bank and SAFE-designated bank for foreign exchange account and FDI registration; State Taxation Administration local tax bureau; local human resources and social security bureau; China Customs and statistics bureau if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is issued, the legal representative must complete mandatory post-incorporation steps. First, obtain approval from the local Public Security Bureau and carve the company seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, and invoice-only seal at an approved engraving shop. Second, open the basic RMB deposit account and any foreign currency account with a commercial bank, and complete SAFE foreign direct investment registration and capital settlement procedures through the bank. Third, complete tax registration with the local State Taxation Administration office, obtain taxpayer identification status, and confirm monthly filing obligations. Fourth, register the company with social insurance and housing fund authorities and enroll all employees. Fifth, if the entity will handle customs declaration or operate bonded logistics, complete customs registration with China Customs. Finally, complete any local statistical or administrative reporting required by the municipal government.
required_dossiers: Business license and unified social credit code certificate
Legal representative identity document
Seal engraving approval from Public Security Bureau
Company articles and shareholder resolution
Bank account opening application forms
SAFE foreign direct investment registration form and settlement confirmation
Tax registration application and taxpayer information form
Social insurance enrollment forms and employee roster
Housing fund registration form
Customs registration certificate if applicable
Statistical registration certificate if required locally
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank account opening is delayed, verify the seal authentication and legal representative presence requirements and re-submit with the original business license; if SAFE registration is queried, provide the underwriter or capital remittance source documents and corrected FDI report; if tax or social insurance filing is late, submit rectification and pay any assessed late fees; if customs registration is not required for pure coordination services, remove it from the scope to avoid unnecessary inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable at formation stage as the WFOE is a project cargo coordination and logistics support company, not a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility; for road movements of oversized OOG cargo, the Ministry of Transport of the People's Republic of China through the provincial highway administration is the operational permitting authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable as a formation-stage industrial license; however, each oversized indivisible load movement requires an Approval Certificate for Transport of Overlimit Goods under the Highway Law and Road Safety Regulations, together with police escort authorization for the approved route, ramp closure permits, and bridge crossing clearance certificates as applicable

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable at formation; if a future staging yard or depot is developed, the competent authority is the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and the local municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for administrative and coordination office use; if a heavy-cargo staging yard, crane pad, or storage depot is later constructed, the project would require an EIA Registration Form for small logistics depots or a full EIA Report / report-form for larger or hazardous cargo storage under the Environmental Impact Assessment Law and the Classified Configuration List for

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局), administered through the provincial/municipal tax service bureaus (主管税务机关) of the entity's registered address; self-service portal: https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn (電子稅務局). For Taiwan-related inbound nexus: Ministry of Finance, Taiwan, Administration of National Taxation — 財政部各地國稅局; portal: https://www.tax.nat.gov.tw.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: The WFOE obtains its 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (統一社會信用代碼) as the statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) upon incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (市場監管總局). STEP 2: Under the multi-certificate consolidation system (多證合一), the STA automatically completes tax registration using the same Unified Social Credit Code; no separate tax registration certificate is issued. STEP 3: The WFOE executes an electronic tax registration supplement at the competent tax service bureau via etax.chinatax.gov.cn to conform VAT taxpayer status (general vs. small-scale), adopt the legal representative's tax identity, and set up the electronic invoice account. STEP 4: For non-resident Taiwan payees or Taiwan PE formation, a separate Taiwan tax registration (稅籍登記) is required under Taiwan's Business Tax Act only when a Taiwan fixed place of business or sales presence arises; otherwise, the Taiwan counterparty bears reverse-charge business tax on imported services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident enterprise 居民企業 under Enterprise Income Tax Law Art. 2; worldwide CIT exposure at 25%; VAT general taxpayer (一般納稅人) by default because WFOEs are incorporated entities with annual sales expected above RMB 5 million; territorial VAT on PRC-sourced service supply; Taiwan business tax does not apply unless a Taiwan PE/fixed place of business is established).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (1) VAT general taxpayer vs. small-scale taxpayer election — small-scale status applies only if annual taxable sales are below RMB 5 million; general taxpayer status is mandatory above the threshold. (2) Zero-rating vs. exemption election for cross-border taxable services (零稅率或免稅選擇) — international transport segments may elect zero-rating with input VAT refund offset under the 免抵退 method, while logistics auxiliary segments are statutorily exempt without refund. (3) Simplified CIT assessment (核定徵收) election is statutorily unavailable for WFOEs engaging in licensed/regulated logistics activities without reliable books. (4) Hybrid mismatch: China's CIT Law Art. 46 and the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (特別納稅調整) override hybrid arrangements; no elective 'check-the-box' regime exists; cross-border payment structures must pass the anti-hybrid substance test.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (增值稅, VAT) in China for the WFOE; Taiwan's Business Tax (加值型及非加值型營業稅, 'VAT/GST hybrid') applies as a destination-jurisdiction levy only if a Taiwan sales presence arises. China VAT is a credit-invoice-method VAT administered under the VAT Law (effective 1 January 2026) and former Provisional VAT Regulations; Taiwan Business Tax is a 5% unidirectional VAT with point-of-import reverse charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: China: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales (RMB 500万) above which general VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory; below this, small-scale VAT taxpayer status at 1%-3% levy. Taiwan: New Taiwan Dollar (TWD) 80,000 average monthly sales threshold for mandatory business tax registration; under TWD 80,000/month the provider is exempt; Taiwan 小規模營業人 pay a 1% deemed profit-based business tax up to TWD 200,000/month. Cross-border reverse-charge: Taiwan recipients of imported services self-assess 5% business tax regardless of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China: Fully digitalized e-invoices (全面數字化的電子發票/數電票) are mandatory for all VAT taxpayers; invoices must be issued through the STA's national electronic invoice service platform (電子發票服務平台) via API or portal integration (金稅四期/Golden Tax IV); real-time tax clearance is required at issuance; the system is a centralized 'tax-control' digital clearance architecture with no physical stamping (stampless 數電票). Taiwan: E-invoice (電子發票) integration with the Ministry of Finance e-invoice platform (財政部電子發票整合服務平台) is mandatory for Taipei/Taoyuan/Kaohsiung/Hsinchu services and all B2B transactions above certain thresholds; cloud-based real-time reporting applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: China zero-rating: (1) Exported goods — 0% VAT with refund of prior-stage input VAT; the WFOE must have actual export customs declarations for the OOG cargo. (2) Cross-border services — zero-rating applies only to international transport services (國際運輸服務) and eligible cross-border services specifically classified as zero-rated under the STA catalogue (財稅〔2016〕36號 Annex 4); for ISIC 5229 project-cargo heavy-haul logistics, the ocean/air international carriage element is zero-rated, whereas logistics auxiliary services (裝卸搬運、貨運代理、打捆加固、倉儲) are VAT-exempt (免稅) without refund entitlement. (3) Eligibility documentation requires the cross-border service contract, proof of service fully rendered to non-PRC recipients, and evidence the consideration is collected from non-PRC parties. Taiwan import note: goods entering Taiwan attract Taiwan 5% business tax at customs unless exempted; Taiwan enterprise zone status does not extend refund rights to PRC-based logistics vendors.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs outward/export declaration form (出口貨物報關單) bearing the customs release stamp and export date
Original ocean or air Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing shipment from PRC customs territory to the Taiwan or overseas destination
Bank foreign-exchange receipt voucher or inward remittance certificate (出口收匯/收結匯水單) proving collection of export proceeds from the non-PRC customer
Zero-rating filing form for cross-border services (跨境應稅行為適用增值稅零稅率免稅備案表) where services are exported
Commercial invoice, packing list, and export sales contract (增值稅發票、裝箱單、出口合同)
OOG project file: axle-load certificates, route/permits for abnormal transport, and port/terminal handling records for heavy-haul cargo

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) as central bank, with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the dedicated foreign exchange regulator exercising delegated oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMB is fully convertible on current account items (trade, services, dividends) subject to genuineness verification and reporting. Capital account items are administered under a positive-list regime; FDI equity injections and shareholder loans require SAFE registration and are confined to designated onshore FX accounts. Profit remittance to the Taiwan shareholder is permissible after annual audit, tax filing, and bank verification, and is generally subject to withholding tax at 10% (reduced to 5% under the Cross-Strait tax cooperation arrangement where the Taiwanese corporate beneficial owner directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE and meets substance/anti-abuse conditions). Remittance can be executed only after payment of enterprise income tax and compliance with the foreign exchange 'round-trip investment' restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China has abolished mandatory export proceeds surrender; the statutory mandatory conversion ratio is zero. All export receipts must nonetheless be repatriated into a designated export receipts foreign exchange account via a SAFE-licensed bank. Under the SAFE Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring framework, ordinary export proceeds must be verified against customs declarations within 90 days of customs clearance; advance receipts must be registered with the bank as 'advance collection' if settlement occurs more than 90 days before export; delayed receipts beyond 90 days require a delayed-collection registration. Failure to repatriate or verify within those windows can trigger administrative penalties and suspension of current-account FX operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for offshore digital EMI banking as a full substitute; an offshore EMI (e.g., Revolut or Airwallex-style platform) is not a licensed domestic settlement institution and cannot host onshore RMB/FCY accounts for the WFOE. Cross-border fintech payment companies may operate only as licensed third-party payment facilitators through a Chinese commercial bank or through a licensed cross-border RMB clearing partner, and they are not permitted to open capital-account FDI escrow accounts. Feasibility rating: Low on all capital-account flows; Medium only for ancillary low-value current-account collections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the WFOE legal representative (and generally the financial controller or authorized person) is required for first-time corporate account opening at all tier-1 Chinese banks. In-branch face-to-face AML interview, original identity documents, company chops, and board resolutions are mandatory; remote online-only onboarding is not accepted for new WFOE accounts. Some banks allow video KYC pre-verification, but a physical in-branch visit remains a de facto mandate for activating the account, particularly for capital escrow accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity or incomplete chain of the Taiwan ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified company registry extracts of the Taiwan shareholder; notarized copies of natural-person UBO passports; full shareholding chain documentation to the ultimate natural persons; board resolution designating the WFOE legal representative; signed AML/UBO declaration under mainland China's beneficial owner registration rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the inbound FDI equity injection from Taiwan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Taiwan parent's audited financial statements for the last three years; six months of Taiwan bank statements for the remitting account; investment approval board resolution; cross-border equity subscription agreement; SAFE Foreign Investment Certificate; capital verification report or bank confirmation of funds in transit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags appearing from OOG heavy-haul logistics invoices, mixed service and reimbursable costs, or high freight invoice values
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master logistics/freight forwarding contracts; itemized commercial invoices and payment schedules; packing lists; bills of lading/airway bills; China customs declaration records; transport insurance certificates; rupture/route certificates for out-of-gauge cargo; subcontractor agreements and payment instructions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or OFAC/UN-screen relevance of Taiwan-based or third-country counterparties involved in project cargo routes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Restricted-party screening outputs from reputable sanctions screening software; cargo end-user and end-use attestations; bill-of-lading and customs entry showing lawful origin and destination; UBO, director, and signatory names cleared against mainland China, UN, EU, and OFAC lists; freight forwarder AEO or customs broker license copies.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires the Taiwan investor to first complete SAMR registration of the WFOE, obtain the Foreign Enterprise Investment Certificate / FDI filing, and open a dedicated RMB or foreign currency Capital Settlement Account (capital escrow account) at a SAFE-designated bank. The equity remittance is transmitted via SWIFT MT103 from the Taiwan bank to the WFOE's capital account using a recognized cross-border remittance purpose code (typically 'Foreign direct investment / equity injection'); the bank carries out pre-entry FDI registration, authenticates the board resolution and investment contract, and credits the funds to the escrow account. Funds may only be released into operational accounts after the bank verifies the capital verification report and actual business use; use of the funds must comply with the negative list for FDI, and no citizen guarantee or security is permitted for Taiwanese inbound investment without full SAFE security registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for heavy-haul project cargo operations (freight carrier payments, port handling, equipment rental, subcontractor settlements, insurance) are executed primarily through onshore bank SWIFT MT103 wire transfers and, for import of capital equipment, through commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) issued by the WFOE's bank. Every outbound payment requires the presenting bank to verify the underlying commercial invoice, contract, customs declaration (for goods), transport evidence and, where relevant, withholding tax certificate. Where the beneficiary is a Taiwan or offshore logistics counterparty, the payment may be denominated in USD, EUR, or RMB under the Cross-Border RMB/CIPS clearing framework; CIPS eliminates intermediate FX conversion costs and shortens clearing time, and is a viable alternative for both MT103 and L/C settlement subject to the bank's cross-border RMB access approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore plain-vanilla FX forward contracts (SAFE-registered, firm deliverable or settled against matching underlying trading exposure)
Onshore FX swaps (for short-term RMB/foreign-currency liquidity management)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (approved by SAFE for balance-sheet and project-debt interest rate/FX management)
Bought plain-vanilla FX options (premium-based, no barrier features; permitted for hedging, selling intrinsic options restricted)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): not available onshore to a domestic WFOE and therefore not permissible as a treasury hedging instrument; NDF markets are confined to offshore counterparties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder consent / general meeting resolution approving the business report, financial statements and profit-appropriation or loss-offsetting proposals
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Taiwan limited company (internal statutory resolution; sourced documents retained at the registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end (no later than 30 June for a calendar-year company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible persons are each fined TWD 10,000–50,000 for failing to procure shareholder consent; continuing default after a rectification order increases fines to TWD 50,000–500,000 and may, if the default persists beyond the prescribed cure period, ground an MOEA dissolution order and deregistration under the Company Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business report, financial statements and profit-appropriation / loss-offsetting proposal filed for record (annual financial statement recordation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) — Company Registration Portal, Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after shareholder consent or annual general meeting approval (by 15 July at the latest for calendar-year consent by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company responsible persons incur fines of TWD 10,000–50,000; uncorrected filings after official notice attract additional fines of TWD 50,000–100,000 with repeated notices; persistent failure constitutes serious statutory non-compliance supporting administrative dissolution/deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of responsible persons and substantive beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) — Beneficial Owner Online Declaration System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 31 January covering the preceding calendar year; any mid-year change in directors, managers or beneficial owners must be declared within 15 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of TWD 50,000–500,000 imposed on responsible persons for refusal to file or for false declarations; continued non-correction after notice may result in dissolution action and cancellation of the company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual operational survey of the foreign-invested enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (investment approval registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the survey window specified by the Investment Commission (commonly issued 1 July–30 September per the annual directive)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to respond triggers a formal cure notice; unresolved omission exposes the company to administrative penalties and may delay or block subsequent foreign-investment approvals, fund remittances and share-transfer registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax settlement return and undistributed-earnings surtax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance) — regional branch with jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Income tax return due 1 May–31 May of the year following the taxable calendar year; undistributed-earnings surtax return due within one month after the settlement period (by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an additional 15% surcharge on assessed tax plus daily interest; understatement or evasion exposes the company to penalties up to three times the underpaid tax, enforced collection measures on bank accounts and, for flagrant taxpayers, judicial restrictions on the business registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit where paid-in capital reaches or exceeds TWD 30 million, where public-company status applies, or where the competent authority (MOEA / National Taxation Bureau) specifically requires certified financial statements; the subject project-cargo logistics WFOE has no statutory license and falls below the threshold unless its paid-in capital is raised above TWD 30 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public Taiwan companies prepare statements under the Commercial Accounting Act supplemented by Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TIFRS) or the SME Accounting Standards; public companies must apply IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the Taiwan WFOE must keep a current register of its responsible persons and substantive beneficial owners and must reconfirm the data each year between 1 January and 31 January on the MOEA online platform; a share transfer that changes beneficial ownership must be declared within 15 days, the register of members must be updated, and China-resident parent transfers require the applicable Investment Commission filing before registration is amended; stale or falsified UBO data exposes the responsible persons to fines of TWD 50,000–500,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$250–1,000 per annum (market rate range in Taiwan for registered-office support, company secretary / registered agent services and routine secretarial filings, excluding CPA and tax-filing fees)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,800–6,000 per annum (estimated fee range for a statutory CPA audit or accountant's certification engagement for a small non-public Taiwan limited-liability WFOE)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard Enterprise Income Tax rate for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise that is a PRC tax resident)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No industry-specific holiday for 5229 project cargo logistics. Generic reliefs: (i) Small and Low-Profit Enterprise (SLE) rate of 5% on taxable income up to RMB 3 million, subject to headcount/assets/turnover tests (policy in force through 2027); (ii) High-and-New-Technology Enterprise (HNTE) 15% rate (not typical for freight/haulage); (iii) Western Region 15% rate if principal operations and headquarters are located in a qualifying western province, which does not apply to a standard WFOE located on the eastern coast.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual: Form A100000 main return within the 'Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return (Category A)' package (approximately 40 schedules), filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax File portal (e-Tax / online Taxpayer Service Platform).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement (annual reconciliation of the four quarterly prepayments)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year WFOE, on or before 31 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross amount of revenue from OOG project cargo services, heavy-haul logistics, freight forwarding, craneage, and escort/other ancillary fees, recorded per PRC Accounting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan-parented WFOE must include all cross-border service fees invoiced to the Taiwan group; exclude equity capital injections and loans. Revenues from offshore-to-onboard RMB milestones must be translated at the PBoC-central parity rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs: subcontractor haulage, vessel/equipment charter, fuel, road permits, port handling, OOG lashing materials, driver and crew labour.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border chartered asset or subcontract payments to the Taiwan parent must be supported by contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation; unsubstantiated group invoices will be adjusted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Office rent, professional fees, IT platforms, safety and ISO certifications, general management payroll.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to the Taiwanese parent are deductible only with actual service substance, contracts and supporting workpapers; otherwise the expense is disregarded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax computed in accordance with the PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Replicate the audited PRC GAAP income statement; schedule A105000 then converts accounting profit into taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted for prohibited deductions, capped deductions, tax-exempt income, and prior-year loss carry-forwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer-pricing adjustments, thin-capitalisation interest disallowances and treaty-based release items are reported on the attached schedules; the Taiwan parent's cost allocations must be eliminated if no invoice exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The positive balance of tax-adjusted income after deducting loss carry-forwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only taxable income of the PRC WFOE enters this line; no consolidation with the Taiwan parent's income is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 26-27 - Tax Rate and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory 25% rate applied; tax payable before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SLE status is claimed, attach the schedule evidencing headcounts below 300, assets below RMB 50 million and taxable income below RMB 3 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 30-34 - Final Tax Due / Extra Payment or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute final liability, subtract quarterly prepayments and withholdings from prior periods; net amount payable is due with the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The remaining withholding on profits to be repatriated to Taiwan is not part of this line; the WFOE reports and pays the 10% dividend WHT in the separate F-series non-resident withholding return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file: RMB 2,000-10,000 per Tax Administration Law Art. 62. Failure to pay assessed tax: daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% (approximately 18.25% per annum) per Art. 32. Underpaid tax from misstatement: 0.5x-5x penalty per Art. 63; the entity is put on the tax non-compliance blacklist, and the legal representative can be blocked from leaving China under Art. 44.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly interim prepayment return: Form A200000 (Enterprise Income Tax Prepayment Return, Category A) through the e-Tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 15 days after the end of each quarter: 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December; Q1-Q3 payments are prepayments, and the fourth quarter is settled through the annual reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated or actual taxable income of the current quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE with Taiwan cross-border transactions must use actual accounting figures and not arbitrary instalments; underpayment of quarterly prepayments attracts the 0.05% daily surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable for the quarter before allowing annual credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No dividend WHT is triggered by the interim return; the WHT arises only at shareholder resolution and payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late Q1-Q3 filing triggers Art. 62 fines of RMB 2,000-10,000 per return; underpayment is subject to the daily 0.05% surcharge from the statutory due date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Related Party Transaction Annual Report (G-series package: 21 schedules) attached to the annual Category A return in the e-Tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same deadline as the annual CIT return: 5 months after fiscal year end (31 May for a calendar-year entity).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the Taiwanese parent, its tax identification, shareholding and organisational structure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Taiwan parent holds 100% of the WFOE, the structure chart, chain percentage and related-party identification must be described completely; omission is treated as documentation failure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual amount of controlled purchases, sales, loans, service fees, IP royalties and other intercompany flows.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separate out cross-strait service revenue of OOG logistics and intragroup charters; amount thresholds trigger Local File preparation if service flows exceed RMB 40 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports the selected arm's length method for each controlled transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the method with highest comparability: TNMM for haulage subcontracting, CUP or Cost Plus for truck hire, Profit Split where risks and functions are interwoven with the Taiwan group.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Missing or false related-party disclosures: administrative fine under TAL Art. 62-63; if contemporaneous documentation is absent, the tax authority may estimate taxable income by reasonable methods and impose a 50% increase of the interest amount under the TP special adjustment rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law for any non-resident enterprise beneficial owner; a Taiwan-resident corporate shareholder normally cannot claim the domestic 5% treaty withholding unless the contested Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement is accepted by the SAT and beneficial ownership is proven.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: If relying on the 2015 Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement (signed 25 Aug 2015, Taiwan's entry into force for fiscal years from 1 Jan 2017; mainland implementation has remained politically obstructed), the WFOE must: (1) obtain a Taiwan Tax Resident Certificate issued by the Ministry of Finance (R.O.C.) in the parent's name; (2) complete the self-assessment 'Information Reporting Form for Treaty Benefits' (SAT Announcement [2019] No. 35) in the annual return workflow before the dividend payment; (3) evidence beneficial ownership and economic substance of the Taiwanese holder under SAT Announcement [2018] No. 9 (staff, premises, functions, risks in Taiwan); (4) retain the board resolution, audited profit calculation and certificate; bank and SAFE will then allow remittance at the lower treaty rate only after the SAT's acceptance; if the SAT challenges the treaty application, the 10% statutory WHT must be withheld within 7 days of the payment and the discrepancy must be settled with interest.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: royalties 10%, interest 10%. Treaty (where the Cross-Strait Agreement is accepted): royalty 5% for a beneficial owner holding at least 25% of capital, otherwise 10%; interest remains capped at 10%, with no inter-bank special rate exemption commonly used; practical application is on a case-by-case and discretionary basis by the competent mainland tax bureau.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory when annual related-party transactions with a party exceed RMB 40 million for services (the relevant limb for OOG haulage, charters and management fees); RMB 200 million for tangible property transfer; RMB 100 million for intangibles and RMB 100 million for financial assets. Master File: mandatory when group-wide consolidated global related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion and the Chinese entity has cross-border controlled transactions. Documentation is due within 5 months of the fiscal year end, simultaneously with the annual CIT return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The PRC has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations as in BVI/UAE. Substance requirements operate through (i) the independent-transaction principle under EIT Law Art. 41 and its Implementation Rules; (ii) the Beneficial Ownership doctrine in SAT Announcement [2018] No. 9, which denies treaty relief to a recipient that lacks real personnel, premises, economic-decision functions and risk-bearing activity; (iii) the general anti-avoidance rule in EIT Law Art. 47; and (iv) the place-of-effective-management test that may relocate the tax status of a nominal Taiwanese entity. A 100% Taiwanese-owned WFOE must maintain actual personnel, payroll, risk-taking, equipment procurement contracts and operational control in Mainland China to retain its deductibility and its status as the source-country taxpayer.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-reporting of OOG project cargo income, back-to-back milestones cash receipts, false subcontractor invoices, or shifting of freight revenue to offshore accounts while maintaining operations in Mainland China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under TAL Art. 63: recovery of the unpaid tax plus 0.05% daily surcharge; administrative penalty of 0.5-5 times the evaded tax; blacklisting on the serious-tax-default list; if the evaded amount exceeds 10% of taxable income and is 'relatively large', the company faces fines under Criminal Law Art. 201 and confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, CFO and finance manager are criminally liable under Criminal Law Art. 201, with imprisonment up to 7 years for huge amounts; travel/exit bans per TAL Art. 44 until the tax is settled; civil liability and disqualification follow if the director signed false statutory accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Missing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging below-cost haulage to the Taiwan parent, paying excess management/royalty fees, or maintaining intercompany balances with no contemporaneous arm's length analysis, while the WFOE stays loss-making.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing reassessment on an arm's length basis may impose additional CIT plus interest at the institutional benchmark rate plus 5 percentage points where Local File/Master File documentation is absent; administrative fines up to RMB 50,000 for failure to preserve documentation; a further 0.5x-5x fraud penalty if false evidence is submitted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve subsidies of cross-border profit diversion to the Taiwanese parent breach fiduciary duty under Company Law Art. 192, exposing them to civil damages; in egregious cases of intentional fund outflows, bank account freezes and exit bans apply; the director could be treated as an accomplice to tax evasion with imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE exists only as a booking entity, with no employees, no leased premises, no project management capability, no risk control, and remits LLC dividends to Taiwan after receiving milestone wire transfers without performing logistics functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Beneficial-ownership denial under SAT Announcement [2018] No. 9, reclassifying the Taiwanese recipient as taxable at the full 10% WHT; the mainland WFOE may be treated as a conduit, with revenue re-attributed to the true owner, resulting in CIT, VAT, fines of 0.5x-5x and possible forced deregistration; the enterprise is removed from the Local Tax Clearance certificate for outbound remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Company Law Art. 23 (2024 revision), the court may pierce the veil and hold the Taiwanese shareholder personally liable for all entity debts and tax arrears; the legal representative's personal ability to exit China is prohibited; if the shell is instrumentalised for evasion, prosecutorial action follows.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing fictitious VAT fapiao from subcontractor entities to inflate OOG haulage costs, or issuing fake intercompany invoices to shift taxable income to the Taiwan parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Law Art. 205: for issuing or obtaining false special VAT invoices, the company is fined and the responsible personnel face imprisonment of 2 years up to life for 'extremely huge' amounts; a simultaneous CIT adjustment with 0.5x-5x penalty is imposed; the entity is added to the serious tax violation database and blocked from export rebates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and CFO face direct criminal liability as the responsible persons of the unit crime, with aggravated sentences where the director ordered or endorsed the fapiao fraud; travel bans and 3-year disqualification from directorship are ancillary.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Cross-Border Foreign Exchange Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Letters of Credit or milestone wires for round-tripping cash, over-invoicing haulage to transfer funds out of China, or splitting large settlements into sub-USD-50,000 tranches to evade outbound tax recordation and AML monitoring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML Law fines up to RMB 5 million for an institution and RMB 500,000 for responsible individuals; foreign-exchange penalties of 0.5-1 times the illegal amount under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations; frozen accounts, mandatory repatriation and loss of banking facilities; criminal money-laundering liability under Criminal Law Art. 191 carries up to 10 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and compliance officer are personally fined, banned from being directors or senior managers for 3 years, subject to exit bans, and, in laundering cases, criminally prosecuted as the controlling person; civil liability for the entity's losses applies.
